messages:
ellie_acme: Hey team — we're seeing a sharp rise in 429s on our account starting ~09:12 UTC. Affects POST /v1/generate for model=redwood-small, roughly 12-18% of requests failing with 429s. No deployment changes on our side. Errors steady for ~30m then spike. Can you help triage? :worried:

maria_support: Thanks @ellie_acme — sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste one or two X-Request-Id values from failed responses? Also let us know if you're on Dedicated or Hosted.

ellie_acme: We're on Hosted. Here's one failed response header dump (redacted):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 04 Nov 2025 09:13:07 GMT
X-Request-Id: 98a2f1c3
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200/min
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 60
Content-Type: application/json
```
Body: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","retry_after":3}

eng_julian: quick checks: 1) that X-RateLimit-Limit looks like a per-account RPM. 1200/min ~ 20 RPS; 2) was throughput concentrated in a short window (burst) or sustained? Any spikes in concurrent requests?

ellie_acme: It looks bursty. We have a couple of worker processes that fan out requests when webhooks arrive. During the incident one webhook handler retried aggressively and spawned ~60 concurrent requests for a few seconds. No other customers report it.

sre_tom: That sounds like a client-side retry/backoff problem — a small number of simultaneous clients creating a thundering herd. Can you share the retry logic? Even a pseudo-snippet helps.

ellie_acme: here's the relevant node snippet we use in prod (simplified):
```js
async function callGen() {
  for (let i=0; i<3; i++) {
    try {
      return await fetch('/v1/generate', {method:'POST', body})
    } catch (e) {
      // immediate retry
    }
  }
}
```
No exponential backoff or jitter.

maria_support: Yep that's the culprit. Immediate retries amplify a transient 429 into a larger incident. Two paths: (A) short-term mitigation -> deploy a client change with exponential backoff + jitter (recommended), or add a per-process concurrency limit; (B) server-side -> we can open a temporary quota bump while you roll out fixes, but that's not a long-term solution.

eng_julian: Adding details for the ops runbook: the platform enforces two throttles — RPM (tokens/min) and TPM (tokens/5min). The bucket refills at RPM/60 per second with a burst capacity of ~3x for short bursts. If your worker fan-out exceeded burst size, tokens went to zero and subsequent retries blocked.

rate-limit-bot: Automatic alert: account=acme-corp reached 100% of configured RPM for route=/v1/generate at 2025-11-04T09:13:05Z. Active throttled connections: 42.

ops_ash: If you want to reproduce locally to test fixes, run this simple script (one-liner):
```
# spawn 50 parallel requests to simulate fan-out
python3 -c "import requests,threading
 def f(): requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', json={'model':'redwood-small'})
 threads=[threading.Thread(target=f) for _ in range(50)]; [t.start() for t in threads]; [t.join() for t in threads]"
```
That will reproduce a short-lived 429 wave if you run it against your account key.

ellie_acme: ok we'll patch the retry. Can you tell us the process to request a temporary increase? We might need a 2x bump for 24h to buy time.

maria_support: To request a short-term bump, open a support ticket with these fields: account_id, owner email, desired RPM and duration, and three example X-Request-Id values. We'll route to Capacity Ops. I can start the request for you if you give me the account_id now.

ellie_acme: account_id: acme-47-prod. Example request ids: 98a2f1c3, d4b6f9e1, a1c7b33f. Requesting 2400/min for 24h.

maria_support: Got it — initiating escalation to Capacity Ops and marking as high priority. In parallel please: 1) deploy retry-with-backoff, 2) add client-side concurrency cap (we recommend <= 10 concurrent requests per worker), 3) instrument X-RateLimit-* headers in logs so future events are faster to diagnose.

eng_julian: For the client fix, sample retry rules we use internally: initial_delay=200ms, multiplier=2, max_delay=10s, full jitter. Example pseudo: 
```
wait = min(max_delay, initial_delay * 2**attempt)
sleep(random.uniform(0, wait))
```
Also avoid re-trying non-idempotent calls without safeguards.

sre_tom: Note about the platform behavior — if we see repeated retry storms from the same API key we may enforce stronger rate limiting or temporary token suspension. So rolling out the backoff ASAP avoids customer-visible throttles.

deploy-bot: Deployment started: acme/webhook-worker v2.14.3 -> prod (canary 10%).

maria_support: Follow-up checklist before closing: - confirm 24h bump approved by Capacity Ops - verify post-deploy 429 rate drops below 0.5% - share logs with X-Request-Id if you see residual 429s - consider using per-route caching / batching if your payloads allow it.

ellie_acme: Thanks all — deploy in progress, will report back in ~15m with metrics. Much appreciated! :heart:

maria_support: Anytime. Ping in this thread when you have the post-deploy numbers and we'll update the ticket.

(End of thread)
